messages.subject: timeinterval issue over New Years
parts:
Hi Mike,

I'm using NicheMapR to model the activity of an ectotherm species. I'm on the tail end of my analysis, but I've just noticed an issue with the model outputs that I'm trying to solve.

I have set timeinterval=365, rather than the default 12, because I would like an output for each day to compare with temperature data I collected in the field. I'm validating modelled vs observed data for each day+time that I have field data, which looks promising. However, I notice that when I have timeinterval at 365, temperature drops by a few degrees on New Years Day, rather than transitioning as expected between the 365th and 1st day. For instance, here's what this looks like with mean daily air temperature overlaid on the activity plot:

 
Here's a snippet of a dataframe that shows the issue. I used this dataframe to create the temperature line in the graph:


Whereas if I set timeinterval=12, the temperature average transitions more smoothly between Dec-Jan, which is consistent with my expectations of this warm summer period. I'm guessing that the model's predictions reset at the start of the year, which is what I'm seeing at timeinterval=365, but that this isn't an issue with timeinterval=12 because temperature has had enough time to build back up by mid-Jan?

Any pointers on what I can do here to better handle these first few days in January?  My current bandaid fix is to just remove the first week of data fram January, but maybe there's a better approach here.

Thanks,
Josh

messages.subject: Re: timeinterval issue over New Years
parts:
Hi Josh,

I see you are running simulations in Australia. That micro_global function uses a monthly climate dataset and splines the monthly data to daily when timeinterval = 365. The jump you see is to do with the spline. I suggest you instead use the new micro_silo function, which uses historical gridded data for Australia. You could do the actual days you have data for that way. Note you just have to put your email address in the micro_silo function as one of the input arguments, which is required to access the SILO data.

Note that the micro_global function will run each day three times to get a 'steady periodic' of soil temperatures (and snow/soil moisture) from the initial conditions, unless timeinterval = 365 in which case it uses the soil temperatures (and snow/soil moisture) of midnight on the previous day as the initial conditions for the next day. So, although you saw a jump in the air temps due to the spline, you should see a smooth transition in soil temps etc. (and local-height air temp if you were modelling air temperatures close to the ground).

I see you have the height of the animal set to 1.4 m and you changed the reference height to 1.4 m as well. Definitely don't do the latter. The Refhyt parameter is the height of your weather data observations. It should stay at the default value (1.2 m for micro_global).

All the best,
Mike

Hi Josh,

I see you are running simulations in Australia. That micro_global function uses a monthly climate dataset and splines the monthly data to daily when timeinterval = 365. The jump you see is to do with the spline. I suggest you instead use the new micro_silo function, which uses historical gridded data for Australia. Note you just have to put your email address in the micro_silo function as one of the input arguments, which is required to access the SILO data.

So, although you saw a jump in the air temps due to the spline, you should see a smooth transition in soil temps etc. (and local-height air temp if you were modelling air temperatures close to the ground).

Hi Josh,

I see you are running simulations in Australia. That micro_global function uses a monthly climate dataset and splines the monthly data to daily when timeinterval = 365. The jump you see is to do with the spline. I suggest you instead use the new micro_silo function, which uses historical gridded data for Australia. You could do the actual days you have data for that way. Note you just have to put your email address in the micro_silo function as one of the input arguments, which is required to access the SILO data.

Note that the micro_global function will run each day three times to get a 'steady periodic' of soil temperatures (and snow/soil moisture) from the initial conditions, unless timeinterval = 365 in which case it uses the soil temperatures (and snow/soil moisture) of midnight on the previous day as the initial conditions for the next day. So, although you saw a jump in the air temps due to the spline, you should see a smooth transition in soil temps etc. (and local-height air temp if you were modelling air temperatures close to the ground).

I see you have the height of the animal set to 1.4 m and you changed the reference height to 1.4 m as well. Definitely don't do the latter. The Refhyt parameter is the height of your weather data observations. It should stay at the default value (1.2 m for micro_global).

All the best,
Mike
